Appellant has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life.

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Indian Penal Code

facts: A written report (Exhibit Ka.1) was submitted at the Polic Station Kotwali.
The complainant, Samay Singh (PW.1), returned home in village Tatarpur from his duty and enquired about his elder daughter Asha (since deceased).
The complainant found the dead body of his daughter Asha inside the field with a Dhoti tied around her neck and another chappal lying near the dead body.
Asha was around 20 years old, and her clothes were blood stained. Her golden ear-rings were missing from her body.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
court_reasoning: The trial court observed that the present case was based on circumstantial evidence.
It was also based on extra judicial confession made by Babu (A-4), one of the accused, in presence of Akhlaq (appellant herein).
The trial court relied upon the statement of PW.1 and PW.2 that Asha had gone to answer nature's call at 1.30 pm.
It also relied upon the evidence of PW.4, Bal Kishan who deposed that he had seen Asha going towards pokhar (pond).
holding: The trial court found Akhlaq (appellant herein) guilty of offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
